entities.summary: Puquios are ancient systems of subterranean aqueducts which allow water to be transported over long distances in hot dry climates without loss of much of the water to evaporation. Puquios are found in the coastal deserts of southern Peru, especially in the Nazca region, and northern Chile. Forty-three puquios in the Nazca region were still in use in the early 21st century and relied upon to bring fresh water for irrigation and domestic use into desert settlements. The origin and dating of the Nazca puquios is disputed, although some archaeologists have estimated that their construction began about 500 CE by indigenous people of the Nazca culture.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Nazca puquios played a crucial role in sustaining desert settlements through their efficient water transportation system, allowing for agriculture and domestic use in arid regions. Their construction, estimated to have begun around 500 CE, demonstrates the ingenuity of indigenous cultures in addressing environmental challenges.
